decisions.reason: The ID Vault was publicly launched with a press release and fits directly into the announced secure identity super-app ecosystem, so management will want to justify that visible commitment.
The identity-bound wallet is central to the payment pillar of the super-app strategy, and its weak visibility can still be blamed on early-stage adoption, so the firm persists.

The NFC tag authenticator is a peripheral, low-visibility add-on with little public commitment, which makes it the most likely candidate for quiet removal, but it still matches the firm's core authentication expertise.
The payment and wallet framework has its own page and is a core building block of the announced platform direction, so the sunk investment and public commitment make continuation very likely.
The multi-service mobile app platform is the embodiment of the firm's super-app strategy, and dropping it would contradict the direction management has announced.
The app shielding library builds on decades of patented application-security expertise and has a dedicated page, making it a committed and strategically anchored offering.
